review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

9:1.sourceText: Εἶχε μὲν οὖν καὶ ἡ πρώτη δικαιώματα λατρείας τό τε ἅγιον κοσμικόν.
9:1.targetText: It had, indeed, then (even the first dwelling place) ordinances of service, also a worldly sanctuary,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness explicitly prints the dwelling/tabernacle noun σκηνή; pinned N1904 has only the first, an inherited substantive designation without a written dwelling noun. The context permits discussion of the first covenant/arrangement, but no source σκηνή is invented here.

9:2.sourceText: σκηνὴ γὰρ κατεσκευάσθη ἡ πρώτη, ἐν ᾗ ἥ τε λυχνία καὶ ἡ τράπεζα καὶ ἡ πρόθεσις τῶν ἄρτων, ἥτις λέγεται Ἅγια·
9:2.targetText: for a dwelling place was prepared, the first, in which was both the lampstand, and the table, and the Bread of the Presentation—which is called “Holy”;

groups.note: The actual presentation-of-the-breads noun phrase is recast as the Bread of the Presentation. Both written nouns and their articles stay in the same constituent despite the inverted head/genitive relation; no distinct Greek bread/presentation head is silently replaced.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the in-which-lampstand/table/presentation nominal description; no corresponding Greek be verb is printed there.

9:3.sourceText: μετὰ δὲ τὸ δεύτερον καταπέτασμα σκηνὴ ἡ λεγομένη Ἅγια ἁγίων,

9:4.sourceText: χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα θυμιατήριον καὶ τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς διαθήκης περικεκαλυμμένην πάντοθεν χρυσίῳ, ἐν ᾗ στάμνος χρυσῆ ἔχουσα τὸ μάννα καὶ ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν ἡ βλαστήσασα καὶ αἱ πλάκες τῆς διαθήκης,
9:4.targetText: having a golden censer, and the Ark of the Covenant overlaid all over with gold, in which [is] the golden pot having the manna, and the rod of Aaron that budded, and the tablets of the covenant,

groups.note: The actual θυμιατήριον is an incense vessel/implement, rendered censer by LSV. Its altar/censer contextual interpretation is not resolved by inventing a different Greek source noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

9:5.sourceText: ὑπεράνω δὲ αὐτῆς Χερουβεὶν δόξης κατασκιάζοντα τὸ ἱλαστήριον· περὶ ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν νῦν λέγειν κατὰ μέρος.
9:5.targetText: and over it cherubim of the glory, overshadowing the propitiatory covering, concerning which we are not to particularly speak now.

groups.note: The actual substantive ἱλαστήριον is the atonement/mercy-seat covering designation, rendered propitiatory covering; no second Greek covering noun is printed.

The actual impersonal singular ἔστιν with a speaking infinitive concerns whether speaking is appropriate/possible here. English recasts its being predicate as plural are in we are to speak; the extra first-person narrator subject is separately explained rather than attributed to a written Greek we pronoun.
The actual κατά μέρος, by part/in detail, is rendered particularly as the complete detail-by-detail adverbial constituent.

unmappedTarget.reason: English explicitly supplies the first-person narrator as subject of the speaking statement. Greek has an impersonal is-to-speak construction without a first-person plural pronoun or agreement form.

9:6.sourceText: Τούτων δὲ οὕτως κατεσκευασμένων εἰς μὲν τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν διὰ παντὸς εἰσίασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὰς λατρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες,
9:6.targetText: And these things having been thus prepared, into the first dwelling place, indeed, the priests go in at all times, performing the services,

groups.note: The actual διὰ παντός is the continually/through-all-time idiom, rendered at all times as a whole constituent.

9:7.sourceText: εἰς δὲ τὴν δευτέραν ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ μόνος ὁ ἀρχιερεύς, οὐ χωρὶς αἵματος, ὃ προσφέρει ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων,
9:7.targetText: and into the second, once in the year, only the chief priest, not apart from blood, which he offers for himself and the errors of the people.

groups.note: The actual ἀγνοήματα names errors/transgressions of ignorance; LSV errors retains that actual noun rather than the different ordinary sins noun.

9:8.sourceText: τοῦτο δηλοῦντος τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Ἁγίου, μήπω πεφανερῶσθαι τὴν τῶν ἁγίων ὁδὸν ἔτι τῆς πρώτης σκηνῆς ἐχούσης στάσιν,
9:8.targetText: By this the Holy Spirit was making evident that the way of the holy [places] has not yet been revealed, the first dwelling place yet having a standing,

groups.note: The actual present declaring participle in a genitive absolute is rendered finite past was making evident with the Holy Spirit subject. The real declaration predicate supports the auxiliary; this does not change the written source into a past finite form.
The actual perfect passive revealing infinitive is the declared proposition, rendered as the finite has been revealed clause in English.
The actual neuter plural holy substantive denotes holy/sanctuary places; bracketed places makes its nominal use explicit without an additional Greek place noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual accusative τοῦτο is the content being made evident, pointing forward to the unrevealed-way proposition. LSV By this naturally points back to the sanctuary arrangement as means. These different attachments/referents are not treated as one exact object identity.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV fronts a by-this means/arrangement relation; pinned N1904 has this as the object/content of making evident, not an instrumental by-this phrase. Same discourse context is insufficient to erase that attachment difference.
English introduces the declarative finite proposition with that; Greek supplies the content as an infinitival clause without a separately written that conjunction.

9:9.sourceText: ἥτις παραβολὴ εἰς τὸν καιρὸν τὸν ἐνεστηκότα, καθ’ ἣν δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίαι προσφέρονται μὴ δυνάμεναι κατὰ συνείδησιν τελειῶσαι τὸν λατρεύοντα,
9:9.targetText: which [is] an allegory in regard to the present time, in which both gifts and sacrifices are offered, which are not able, in regard to conscience, to make perfect him who is serving,

groups.note: The actual feminine plural being-able participle qualifies the offerings; LSV expands that same verbal modifier as which are able, retaining its actual predicate rather than inventing a separate relative pronoun or be head.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

Source-witness attachment difference: pinned καθ’ ἣν has a feminine relative referring to the allegory/arrangement; LSV in which follows the masculine-time reading/construal after present time. The different relative attachment is not collapsed into an exact phrase identity.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness attachment difference: LSV refers to the present time by in which, while pinned N1904 καθ’ ἣν is feminine referring to the allegory/arrangement; the changed attachment and relation remain explicit.

9:10.sourceText: μόνον ἐπὶ βρώμασιν καὶ πόμασιν καὶ διαφόροις βαπτισμοῖς, δικαιώματα σαρκὸς μέχρι καιροῦ διορθώσεως ἐπικείμενα.
9:10.targetText: only on the basis of food, and drinks, and different immersions, and fleshly ordinances—until the time of reformation imposed on [them].

groups.note: The actual genitive flesh noun qualifies the ordinances; English renders that flesh relation adjectivally as fleshly, without a separately written σαρκικός adjective.
The actual passive imposing/lying-upon participle supplies imposed on; the English recipient them remains supplied because the source prints no corresponding recipient expression.

unmappedTarget.reason: The longer witness coordinates the ordinances with an extra and; pinned N1904 directly apposes the fleshly ordinances without that additional conjunction.
English supplies a recipient of the imposed ordinances. Pinned N1904 prints the imposed participle without an explicit recipient pronoun; no unrelated prior person is borrowed as this object.

9:11.sourceText: Χριστὸς δὲ παραγενόμενος ἀρχιερεὺς τῶν γενομένων ἀγαθῶν, διὰ τῆς μείζονος καὶ τελειοτέρας σκηνῆς οὐ χειροποιήτου, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν οὐ ταύτης τῆς κτίσεως,
9:11.targetText: But Christ having come, Chief Priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect dwelling place not made with hands—that is, not of this creation—

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness predicate difference: pinned γενομένων is the having-come/become good things; LSV coming follows the future/prospective μελλόντων reading. The actual becoming and prospective coming predicate identities are not interchanged.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness predicate difference: LSV follows μελλόντων, prospective coming good things; pinned N1904 γενομένων describes the things that have come. No prospective source predicate is invented.

9:12.sourceText: οὐδὲ δι’ αἵματος τράγων καὶ μόσχων, διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος, εἰσῆλθεν ἐφάπαξ εἰς τὰ ἅγια, αἰωνίαν λύτρωσιν εὑράμενος.

groups.note: The actual explicit ἐφάπαξ adverb supplies once, independently of the entered verb tense. This pairing does not infer once-for-all scope merely from an aorist form.

9:13.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ τὸ αἷμα τράγων καὶ ταύρων καὶ σποδὸς δαμάλεως ῥαντίζουσα τοὺς κεκοινωμένους ἁγιάζει πρὸς τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς καθαρότητα,

9:14.sourceText: πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ αἷμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς διὰ Πνεύματος αἰωνίου ἑαυτὸν προσήνεγκεν ἄμωμον τῷ Θεῷ, καθαριεῖ τὴν συνείδησιν ἡμῶν ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων εἰς τὸ λατρεύειν Θεῷ ζῶντι.

Source-witness person difference: pinned ἡμῶν is our, first person plural; LSV your follows the second-person ὑμῶν reading. The possessors are not relabeled as the same pronoun.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness person difference: LSV second-person your corresponds to ὑμῶν, whereas pinned N1904 prints first-person ἡμῶν, our.

9:15.sourceText: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο διαθήκης καινῆς μεσίτης ἐστίν, ὅπως θανάτου γενομένου εἰς ἀπολύτρωσιν τῶν ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ παραβάσεων τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν λάβωσιν οἱ κεκλημένοι τῆς αἰωνίου κληρονομίας.
9:15.targetText: And because of this, He is mediator of a new covenant, that [His] death having come for redemption of the transgressions under the first covenant, those called may receive the promise of the continuous inheritance,

unmappedTarget.reason: English specifies the death as His; pinned N1904 has the death-having-occurred genitive absolute without a written possessor pronoun.

9:16.sourceText: ὅπου γὰρ διαθήκη, θάνατον ἀνάγκη φέρεσθαι τοῦ διαθεμένου·
9:16.targetText: for where a covenant [is], [it is] necessary to establish the death of the [one] having made [it],

groups.note: The actual covenant/will noun is also the object understood with the immediately following maker/disposer participle. English resumes that same arrangement as bracketed it; no second written Greek object pronoun is claimed. Διαθήκη can denote covenant or testament/will, and the pairing preserves the actual word without deciding between those legal/contextual interpretations.

The actual passive φέρεσθαι means to be brought forward/reported, here concerning death (Thayer5342). English to establish recasts that evidentiary bringing-forward of death; it does not print a different Greek establishing verb or preserve passive voice in English.

The actual article plus middle arranging/disposal participle identifies the person who made the covenant/will. English one supplies that real nominalized person construction; no separate Greek one noun or ordinary ποιέω making lemma is invented.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

9:17.sourceText: διαθήκη γὰρ ἐπὶ νεκροῖς βεβαία, ἐπεὶ μή ποτε ἰσχύει ὅτε ζῇ ὁ διαθέμενος.
9:17.targetText: for a covenant is affirmed at death, since it is not in force at all when the [one] having made [it] lives,

groups.note: The actual covenant/will is the arrangement understood as object of its maker/disposer participle in this same statement. English resumes it as bracketed it with having made, retaining that actual arrangement without a second original pronoun.

The actual ἐπὶ νεκροῖς says in the case of deceased persons. LSV at death turns that dead-person condition into the corresponding death-event/state wording; no separate Greek θάνατος noun is printed in this phrase.
The actual βεβαία is an adjective, firm/valid, rendered affirmed. Its English is remains a supplied copula; the source does not print a passive βεβαιόω affirming verb.
The actual μή ποτε gives the never/not-at-any-time negative scope, rendered not ... at all as a whole negative-time constituent.
The actual finite ἰσχύει means is effective/in force; its one real validity/strength predicate supports the English it is in force, not an invented separate be head.
The actual article with the middle disposal/arranging participle designates the maker of the covenant/will. English the one having made expresses that real substantive person construction.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

9:28.sourceText: οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστός, ἅπαξ προσενεχθεὶς εἰς τὸ πολλῶν ἀνενεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας, ἐκ δευτέρου χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας ὀφθήσεται τοῖς αὐτὸν ἀπεκδεχομένοις εἰς σωτηρίαν.
